leadIn: After completing this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Implement a basic switch statement that handles all possible cases for a union type.
Apply the `never` type to represent code that should never be executed.
Construct an exhaustive switch by adding a default case that assigns the remaining value to a variable of type `never`.
Configure TypeScript to produce a compile-time error when a new case is added to the union but not handled in the switch.
Manipulate a union type by adding new members and observing the resulting type errors.
Initialize a variable with a union type and use it in an exhaustive switch statement.
Integrate an exhaustive switch pattern into a function that returns different values based on the input type.
